subject.title: fix(embeddings): bound openai-compatible requests without AbortSignal

question: Should unsignaled OpenAI-compatible gateway and capability calls use runtime-owned 60-second query and 10-minute batch deadlines, or should the provider permanently impose the new 60-second and 120-second transport policy?
rationale: Both choices prevent indefinite hangs, but they define different latency and upgrade contracts for existing slow endpoints; repository evidence does not establish that shortening the advertised 10-minute batch window is intentional.

options.title: Use Runtime-Owned Deadlines
options.body: Have gateway and capability callers construct signals from provider runtime metadata so each operation has one authoritative deadline and existing longer batch behavior remains available.

options.title: Align Provider Failsafes
options.body: Keep provider-level defaults but align them with the existing query and 10-minute batch runtime budgets, with focused tests proving the hierarchy.

options.title: Adopt The New Caps
options.body: Accept 60-second query and 120-second batch limits as a deliberate compatibility change and document and prove the upgrade impact for slow endpoints.

recommendation.title: Use Runtime-Owned Deadlines
recommendation.body: Have gateway and capability callers construct signals from provider runtime metadata so each operation has one authoritative deadline and existing longer batch behavior remains available.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged integration and refactor history most directly owns the current provider-runtime contract.
